the capture that leaves the two lone Kings draws immediately (insufficient); the captured rook sits inert in the hand

the General captures like a Chariot; taking the last piece leaves the two lone Generals — insufficient. The black General sits on a8, off the shared file: two Generals facing each other across an open file is an illegal state (the side that just moved would stand in check — the flying-general prohibition, as in xiangqi)
cross-variant: a lone King versus a lone General is declared drawn by insufficient material outright (deciders' ruling, 2026-07-10 — not strictly a dead position, but no side can force a win)
ōgi: capturing the last piece converts it into the hand — droppable material remains, so lone-Kings-on-the-board is NOT insufficient here
second is fully jammed (pawns on/against their last rank, king walled in by them): an empty PSEUDO-legal set — the nomove draw, not a stalemate
the knight checks the jammed king: still the nomove draw — an empty pseudo-legal set outranks checkmate (terminal::classify)
the just-double-stepped -p checks the King; the en-passant capture removes the checker and is legal — pins the marker-reading escape (ADR-0010 finding 3)
xiongqi lateral en passant — the marked Soldier-victim behind the skipped square is captured into the tray
xiongqi lateral en passant that would expose the capturer's royal (crafted `-` marker): the capture reading is decisive — illegal (LeavesRoyalInCheck)
xiongqi sideways step beside an UNMARKED double-stepper: a quiet move — the victim stays (deciders' confirmation, 2026-07-19)
canonicality — the double step f2-f4 is NOT marked `-P`: capturing en passant would vacate e3 and open the e-file (Q e2 → g^ e8), a self-check for the capturer
the e3 Soldier is functionally pinned by Q e2 against g^ e8: the sideways step opens the e-file (LeavesRoyalInCheck)
the pinned Soldier's only move: capturing the pinning Queen forward — the capture checks K^ e1 (Soldier attack + royal confrontation on the opened e-file → `-K^`), Queen inert in hand
canonicality — the double step f2-f4 IS marked `-P`: the e3 Soldier can capture en passant without exposing its General
the sideways step onto the skipped square IS the en-passant capture (mandatory): the marked `-P` leaves f4, and the opened e-file puts K^ in check by g^ (royal confrontation → `-K^`)
canonicality — the double step f2-f4 is NOT marked `-P`: removing the f4 victim would open the c1-Bishop's diagonal to g^ h6, a self-check for the capturer
beside the UNMARKED f4 pawn the sideways step is a quiet move — nothing is removed (the diagonal to g^ h6 stays blocked by f4, so the step itself is safe)

pure ōgi performs NO dead-position detection (rules-of-ogi §Dead-Position Detection): even the materially dead lone-Kings-with-empty-hands configuration (unreachable from the standard start) does not end the game
chess: the capture that leaves King + Bishop versus King is an immediate dead-position draw (rules-of-chess §Dead-Position Detection)
chess: the capture that leaves King + Knight versus King is an immediate dead-position draw
chess: Kings and Bishops only, all Bishops on the same colour (B h1, b c8) — dead as soon as the last other piece is captured
chess: Bishops on OPPOSITE colours (B h1, b b8) are not a dead position — a cooperative mate exists, the game continues
chess: King + two Knights versus King is NOT dead (the criterion is possibility, not forceability — a cooperative mate exists), the game continues
ōgi kingside castling — e1-g1, adopted 2026-07-27 (rules-of-ogi §Castling): the Rook relocates to f1 and, having moved, goes plain R
ōgi queenside castling — e1-c1: the Rook relocates to d1
ōgi castling with a rights-less Rook is illegal: the h1 Rook is plain R — it has moved, or was dropped from hand (a drop never confers castling rights; rules-of-ogi §Castling)
canonicality — a gote Bishop dropped on g2 attacks f1, the King's transit square: the canonicalizer flips the h1 Rook +R -> -R (right retained, castling temporarily blocked)
ōgi castling through the attacked transit square f1 (Bishop g2) is illegal — the -R marker announces exactly this blocked state
xiongqi kingside castling — e1-g1, adopted 2026-07-27 (rules-of-xiongqi §Castling): the Chariot relocates to f1; the enemy General sits off the e/g-files so no flying-general line interferes
xiongqi queenside castling — e1-c1: the Chariot relocates to d1

a two-file General displacement onto an OCCUPIED square is a Chariot-style capture, not castling: no Chariot relocation, the knight goes inert into the hand, and the General's displacement strips h1 to plain R (rules-of-xiongqi §Castling, disambiguation)
flying general — the landing square g1 lies on the enemy General's open g-file (condition 6): castling is illegal, and the h1 Chariot canonically carries -R
the Bear (熊) slides any number of squares diagonally, exactly as a Western Bishop — here two squares within Red's own half
the river restricts ONLY Soldiers: the Bear slides straight across it, unlike the xiàngqí Elephant it replaces, which may never leave its own half
the Bear is a slider, not a jumper: an occupied square on the diagonal blocks it
the Bear's domain is the diagonal alone — the orthogonal slide belongs to the Chariot

the Empress (妃/騛) combines Chariot and Knight; here the Chariot component slides the full file. The lone black Soldier on h4 is deliberate: without a second black piece, an Empress on d7 covers both a7 (rank) and b8 (knight jump) and the bare General is STALEMATED — the vector would then test the terminal classifier rather than the slide
the Knight component jumps: the Empress reaches f2 from d1 with BOTH intervening squares occupied (its own General on e1, its own Soldier on e2)
the Chariot component is a slider: a piece on the file blocks it (only the Knight component jumps)
the Empress is Chariot+Knight, NOT Chariot+Bear: it has no diagonal slide at all — the single sharpest difference from the Western Queen it replaces
a Red Soldier on rank 3 has not crossed the river (the midline between ranks 4 and 5), so it has no sideways step yet
past the river (Red on ranks 5-8) the Soldier gains the one-square sideways step onto an empty square — the river's only effect in the whole game
the Soldier captures straight forward only — never diagonally, at any point of the board, crossed river or not (unlike the chess Pawn)
a Soldier still carrying the `+` prefix may advance two squares straight forward when both squares are empty
promotion is mandatory on the last rank and the target is the player's genuine CHOICE among four pieces; the move record must carry it as the actor
the same Soldier on the same square promotes to a Knight instead — proving the choice is real and not a fixed transformation (contrast the ōgi Fu, whose Tokin promotion is forced and actorless)
the four targets are Chariot, Knight, Bear and Empress: a Soldier may never become the royal piece
promotion is mandatory: the Soldier may not decline it by naming its own kind
